edges.description: The olfactory bulb is the most frequent single site of Lewy pathology and the earliest stage in the unified staging scheme.
edges.source: Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation and Lewy Body Formation

edges.description: Lewy body diseases degenerate the basal forebrain cholinergic neurons themselves. Loss is early in DLB and starts in the posterior cell groups.
edges.source: Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation and Lewy Body Formation

edges.description: Lewy and Alzheimer pathologies co-occur and interact. Higher AD neuropathology goes with higher cerebral alpha-synuclein scores; the direction of causation between the two is not established.
edges.source: Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation and Lewy Body Formation

edges.description: Lewy pathology in postganglionic sympathetic axons leads to their distal-first degeneration in the heart.
edges.source: Peripheral Autonomic and Lower Brainstem Lewy Pathology

edges.description: Enteric and vagal Lewy pathology is the proposed substrate of early constipation. The lesions are documented in DLB, but no DLB study relates lesion burden to constipation, and immobility and anticholinergic medication are competing causes.
edges.source: Peripheral Autonomic and Lower Brainstem Lewy Pathology

edges.description: Detrusor overactivity is nearly universal in DLB, but whether it comes from autonomic, pontine or frontal Lewy pathology has not been tested.
edges.source: Peripheral Autonomic and Lower Brainstem Lewy Pathology

edges.description: Ascending from the medulla, Lewy pathology reaches the pontine tegmentum ahead of the substantia nigra and cortex.
edges.source: Peripheral Autonomic and Lower Brainstem Lewy Pathology

edges.description: Sympathetic noradrenergic failure removes the vasoconstrictor response to standing. Cardiac denervation is the measurable marker of this wider sympathetic failure; orthostatic hypotension in DLB is intermediate in severity between Parkinson disease and multiple system atrophy.
Olfactory bulb pathology impairs smell identification, which is more severe in DLB than in AD and appears earlier.
In the brain-first route, pathology spreads from the olfactory bulb into the amygdala and connected limbic regions.
Loss of the descending REM-on output removes the inhibition of skeletal motor neurons during REM sleep.
intermediate_mechanisms: loss of descending glutamatergic drive to medullary and spinal inhibitory premotor neurons

edges.description: Continued rostral spread reaches the substantia nigra after the pontine tegmentum, so parkinsonism typically follows RBD.
In the caudo-rostral sequence, pathology ascends from the pontine tegmentum through the midbrain to the limbic lobe.
With atonia lost, motor programmes generated during dreaming are enacted.
Nigral neuron loss removes dopaminergic input to the putamen. Striatal DAT binding on imaging tracks nigral neuron density rather than Lewy, tau or amyloid burden.
edges.target: Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation

edges.description: Striatal dopamine loss produces the bradykinetic-rigid motor syndrome, which in DLB is dominated by postural instability and gait difficulty.
edges.source: Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation
Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation
Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation

edges.description: With dopaminergic reserve depleted and no D2 receptor upregulation, D2 blockade by an antipsychotic produces severe extrapyramidal and sensitivity reactions. The receptor mechanism rests on post-mortem series and has not been tested in vivo.
intermediate_mechanisms: failure of striatal D2 receptor upregulation
D2 receptor blockade on a depleted dopaminergic system
edges.source: Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation

edges.description: Loss of basal forebrain neurons removes cholinergic terminals across cortex, limbic system and thalamus.
Depletion of nucleus basalis neurons is associated with daytime sleepiness that is independent of night-time sleep fragmentation.

Cortical ChAT loss is greater in hallucinating patients, and loss of alpha7 nicotinic binding in temporal cortex goes with hallucinations. Cholinesterase inhibitors reduce hallucinations, the interventional support for this edge.
The midfrontal cholinergic deficit, more than a hippocampal one, distinguishes Lewy body dementia from AD, and cholinesterase inhibition improves attention-heavy tasks.
Cholinesterase inhibitors reduce delusions, but no lesion study ties a cholinergic measure to delusions specifically.
Apathy improves on cholinesterase inhibitors, a secondary trial endpoint. No lesion or imaging study of apathy in DLB was found.

Postural instability and gait difficulty dominate the DLB motor syndrome more than in Parkinson disease, and a cholinergic contribution is proposed. The pedunculopontine cholinergic neurons that carry this role in Parkinson disease are not significantly reduced in DLB, so the responsible cholinergic lesion is unknown.
Proposed but unproven. Cortical ChAT does not differ by fluctuation status; fluctuation-related signals are thalamic and electrophysiological.
Cholinergic terminals are lost in the thalamus as well as cortex, and thalamic nicotinic receptor binding differs between patients with and without disturbed consciousness.
Thalamic and electrophysiological measures track fluctuation severity.
Misidentification syndromes map to limbic and paralimbic hypoperfusion. The evidence is perfusion imaging rather than histopathology.
Progression from the limbic (transitional) to the diffuse neocortical stage, which carries a shorter illness.
Occipital hypometabolism on FDG-PET correlates with visual cortex neuropathology. Whether the hypometabolism is primarily synaptic or cholinergic is unresolved.
edges.target: Occipital and Parietal Association Cortex Dysfunction

edges.description: Alpha-synuclein burden independently predicts a shorter illness, consistent with neocortical Lewy pathology driving neurodegeneration.

edges.source: Occipital and Parietal Association Cortex Dysfunction
Occipital and Parietal Association Cortex Dysfunction
Occipital and Parietal Association Cortex Dysfunction

edges.description: Medial temporal tangle pathology produces the amnestic deficit that is relatively mild in pure Lewy body disease.
AD co-pathology accelerates decline and shortens survival.
Illusions and presence phenomena come before well-formed hallucinations in time. Whether they are an early form of the same process or a separate marker of susceptibility is not settled.
Parkinsonism is the main clinical risk factor for the recurrent falls of DLB.
Slower gait raises fall risk in DLB.

Cases were markedly less likely than matched controls to use caffeine, with the strongest inverse association reported for any exposure in this disease. Pointed at the defining Lewy body pathology with intermediates unknown, because the study is a retrospective case-control risk-factor analysis and measures no mechanistic endpoint. The effect size is larger than the corresponding caffeine association in Parkinson disease, and reverse causation is a stronger objection here than there: caffeine intake falls in the prodromal period, and exposure was ascertained from records and informants after diagnosis.

nodes.description: DLB is characterized morphologically by widespread cortical and subcortical alpha-synuclein aggregation forming Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites. The aggregation process runs for years before the full clinical syndrome, and the regions it reaches first determine which features appear first. In this pathograph the aggregation hub feeds the anatomical spread stages (peripheral autonomic and lower brainstem, olfactory bulb, then midbrain and basal forebrain, then limbic and neocortical), each of which carries the phenotypes of its phase.
nodes.id: Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation and Lewy Body Formation

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.
evidence.snippet: Both are characterized morphologically by widespread cortical and subcortical α-synuclein/Lewy body plus β-amyloid and tau pathologies.

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: There is a variable progression of α-synuclein aggregation many years before the full DLB syndrome develops,e1 which likely determines the pattern of early clinical changes.

evidence.reference_title: Prodromal Dementia With Lewy Bodies: Evolution of Symptoms and Predictors of Dementia Onset.
evidence.snippet: Apathy, depression, and anxiety were common prodromal neuropsychiatric symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Survival and causes of death among people with clinically diagnosed dementia with Lewy bodies: A multicenter cohort study.
evidence.snippet: Failure to thrive (stopped eating, drinking) or multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) maybe the most common cause of death (41.7%), followed by pneumonia or aspiration (29.2%).

evidence.reference_title: Cause of Death and End-of-Life Experiences in Individuals with Dementia with Lewy Bodies.
evidence.snippet: Failure to thrive was the most common cause of death (65%), followed by pneumonia and swallowing difficulties (23%), other medical conditions (19%), and complications from falling (10%) (multiple causes allowed).

evidence.reference_title: Influence of pneumonia complications on the prognosis of patients with autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and vascular dementia.
evidence.snippet: Pneumonia complication was observed with high incidence in each subtype of dementia, especially in DLB (90.5%).

nodes.description: Impaired autophagy and lysosomal functions are central to DLB pathogenesis. Neurons are particularly vulnerable to autophagy-lysosomal defects due to their postmitotic nature and polarized morphologies. Mutations in genes regulating autophagy and lysosomal functions, particularly GBA, contribute to impaired clearance of alpha-synuclein aggregates and damaged organelles. This dysfunction creates a vicious cycle where accumulating protein aggregates further impair the autophagic-lysosomal system.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms of autophagy-lysosome dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence.snippet: Autophagy is a lysosome-based degradative process used to recycle obsolete cellular constituents and eliminate damaged organelles and aggregate-prone proteins. Their postmitotic nature and extremely polarized morphologies make neurons particularly vulnerable to disruptions caused by autophagy-lysosomal defects, especially as the brain ages.

evidence.reference_title: Current strategies in the management of dementia with lewy bodies and future directions based on disease pathophysiology.
evidence.snippet: In particular, we highlight antibody-based therapies to attenuate protein aggregation, compounds that enhance the generation of cellular energy and autophagy-enhancing agents as particular areas of promise.

evidence.reference_title: The Genetics of Dementia with Lewy Bodies: Current Understanding and Future Directions.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in GBA reduce activity of its lysosomal enzyme, β-glucocerebrosidase (Gcase)

nodes.description: Degeneration of the cholinergic neurons of the nucleus basalis of Meynert. It is already present early in DLB, begins in the posterior basal forebrain cell groups, and in vivo nucleus basalis atrophy is comparable to that in AD. Neuronal depletion here is also associated with excessive daytime sleepiness.

evidence.reference_title: Atrophy of the cholinergic basal forebrain in dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease dementia.
evidence.snippet: The DLB group demonstrated pronounced and subregion-specific atrophy of the BF which was comparable to BF atrophy in AD: volume of the nucleus basalis Meynert was significantly reduced by 20-25%, whereas rostral BF nuclei were only marginally affected.

evidence.reference_title: Cholinergic white matter pathways in dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: Patients who have dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease show early degeneration of the cholinergic nucleus basalis of Meynert.

evidence.reference_title: Cholinergic changes in Lewy body disease: implications for presentation, progression and subtypes.
evidence.snippet: This implies that posterior cholinergic cell groups in the basal forebrain are affected in the early stages of Lewy body disorders, while more anterior regions are typically affected later in the disease progression.

evidence.reference_title: Comparison of extrapyramidal signs in dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: The 58 DLB patients with complete data had more severe action tremor, body bradykinesia, difficulty arising from a chair, and facial expression, gait, and rigidity symptoms than PD patients (all P<0.001). Abnormal posture and tremor at rest did not differ.

evidence.reference_title: Risk factors for dementia with Lewy bodies: a case-control study.
evidence.snippet: CONCLUSION: DLB risk factors are an amalgam of those for AD and PD.

nodes.description: Loss of postganglionic cardiac sympathetic axons, distal-first, ahead of neuronal loss in the sympathetic ganglia. It is measured as reduced cardiac 123I-MIBG uptake, which is already reduced in mild DLB. Together with wider sympathetic failure it underlies orthostatic hypotension.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sympathetic denervation precedes neuronal loss in the sympathetic ganglia in Lewy body disease.
evidence.snippet: Decreased cardiac uptake of MIBG in Lewy body disease reflects actual cardiac sympathetic denervation, which precedes the neuronal loss in the sympathetic ganglia.

evidence.reference_title: Quantitative correlation between cardiac MIBG uptake and remaining axons in the cardiac sympathetic nerve in Lewy body disease.
evidence.snippet: Tight quantitative correlation between cardiac (123)I-MIBG uptake and corresponding loss of sympathetic axons in LBD, as established for the first time by this study

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic accuracy of 123I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine myocardial scintigraphy in dementia with Lewy bodies: a multicenter study.
evidence.snippet: In a subpopulation of patients with mild dementia (MMSE ≥ 22, n = 47), the sensitivity and specificity were 77.4% and 93.8%, respectively, with the delayed heart-to-mediastinum ratio

nodes.description: Rivastigmine and donepezil are used for cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Randomised trials show benefit on attention-heavy cognition, hallucinations, delusions and apathy, but the confirmatory phase 3 donepezil trial did not meet its co-primary endpoints, and benefits fade on discontinuation.

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.
evidence.snippet: Clinical management of both disorders includes cholinesterase inhibitors, other pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic strategies, but these have only a mild symptomatic effect.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Meta-analyses of Class I clinical trials of rivastigmine and donepezil support the use of cholinesterase inhibitors (CHEIs) in DLB for improving cognition, global function, and activities of living

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of rivastigmine in dementia with Lewy bodies: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled international study.
evidence.snippet: Patients taking rivastigmine were significantly less apathetic and anxious, and had fewer delusions and hallucinations while on treatment than controls.

evidence.reference_title: Donepezil for dementia with Lewy bodies: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: Donepezil at 5 and 10mg/day produces significant cognitive, behavioral, and global improvements that last at least 12 weeks in DLB patients, reducing caregiver burden at the highest dose.

evidence.reference_title: Donepezil for dementia with Lewy bodies: a randomized, placebo-controlled, confirmatory phase III trial.
evidence.snippet: The co-primary endpoints were not achieved in this trial.

nodes.description: Neocortical neurofibrillary tangles and neuritic plaques, present in many DLB cases. Tangle burden shifts the phenotype toward AD: the DLB syndrome emerges later or not at all, hallucinations are less frequent, memory is more impaired, and decline and death come sooner. DLB with RBD carries less of it.

evidence.reference_title: Influence of Alzheimer pathology on clinical diagnostic accuracy in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: The low Braak stage (0 to 2, n = 24) subjects had a higher frequency of visual hallucinations (65%) than did subjects with DLB with higher (3 to 6, n = 66) Braak stages (33%, p = 0.008), and showed a slightly greater but not significant degree of EPS.

evidence.reference_title: Subtypes of dementia with Lewy bodies are associated with α-synuclein and tau distribution.
evidence.snippet: TLBD with neocortical tangles had 48% diagnostic sensitivity for probable DLB and 52% for the DLB syndrome, with median latencies >6 years from cognitive onset, and were cognitively similar to AD.

evidence.reference_title: Neuropathological and genetic correlates of survival and dementia onset in synucleinopathies: a retrospective analysis.
evidence.snippet: Alzheimer's disease neuropathology is common in synucleinopathies and confers a worse prognosis for each increasing level of neuropathological change.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder and subtypes in autopsy-confirmed dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: These patients also had a lower Braak neurofibrillary tangle stage (stage IV vs stage VI) and lower neuritic plaque scores (18% vs 85% frequency), but no difference in Lewy body distribution.

evidence.reference_title: The prevalence of autonomic symptoms in dementia and their association with physical activity, activities of daily living and quality of life.
evidence.snippet: Total autonomic symptom scores, urinary symptoms, constipation and postural dizziness were significantly higher in PDD, DLB and VAD patients than either controls or AD patients

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective survey of prodromal symptoms in dementia with Lewy bodies: comparison with Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: DLB patients exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of olfactory dysfunction, constipation, increased saliva and signs of rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder at the onset of memory loss than AD patients and normal controls.

nodes.description: Loss of neocortical choline acetyltransferase activity, more severe and earlier than in AD and independent of coexisting AD pathology, together with reduced cortical acetylcholinesterase and alpha7 nicotinic receptor binding. It is the best-supported substrate of visual hallucinations and of the attentional deficit, and the target of cholinesterase inhibitors.

evidence.reference_title: Cholinergic dysfunction in diseases with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Mean midfrontal ChAT activity was markedly reduced in diseases with LB (LBV: 53.3 +/- 39.0; PD: 54.8 +/- 35.7; DLBD: 41.3 +/- 24.8) compared to NC (255.4 +/- 134.6; p < 0.001) and AD (122.6 +/- 78.9; p < 0.05).

evidence.reference_title: Early and widespread cholinergic losses differentiate dementia with Lewy bodies from Alzheimer disease.
evidence.snippet: Although cholinergic deficits are seen in both AD and LBV, loss of ChAT activity is less severe and occurs later in the clinical course of AD. Conversely, in LBV, loss of ChAT activity is already prominent in the earliest stages of the illness

evidence.reference_title: Mapping of brain acetylcholinesterase alterations in Lewy body disease by PET.
evidence.snippet: Patients with PDD/DLB, however, had even lower AChE activity in the cerebral cortex (% reduction = -27%) (p < 0.01).

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Symptoms include hallucinations in visual and in other modalities and systematized delusions including Capgras syndrome,55 apathy, anxiety, and depression.

evidence.reference_title: Psychiatric morbidity in dementia with Lewy bodies: a prospective clinical and neuropathological comparative study with Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: Hallucinations, depression, delusions, and delusional misidentification were all significantly higher for patients with dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Psychiatric morbidity in dementia with Lewy bodies: a prospective clinical and neuropathological comparative study with Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: Hallucinations, depression, delusions, and delusional misidentification were all significantly higher for patients with dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Neural correlates of psychotic symptoms in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: misidentifications were related to dysfunction of the limbic-paralimbic structures and delusions were related to dysfunction of the frontal cortices

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.
evidence.snippet: The clinical features of DLB and PDD include cognitive impairment, parkinsonism, visual hallucinations, and fluctuating attention.

evidence.reference_title: Long-Term Cognitive Decline in Dementia with Lewy Bodies in a Large Multicenter, International Cohort.
evidence.snippet: The mean annual decline in MMSE score was 2.1 points in DLB, compared to 1.6 in AD (p = 0.07 compared to DLB) and 1.8 in PDD (p = 0.19).

evidence.reference_title: Survival time and differences between dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease following diagnosis: A meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
evidence.snippet: Average survival time in DLB from diagnosis was 4.11 years (SD ± 4.10) and in AD 5.66 (SD ± 5.32) years, equating to a 1.60 (95% CI: -2.44 to -0.77) years shorter survival in DLB (p < 0.01).

evidence.reference_title: Dysphagia in Lewy body dementia - a clinical observational study of swallowing function by videofluoroscopic examination.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-six patients (32%) reported symptoms of dysphagia such as swallowing difficulties or coughing. Twenty-four (92%) of these had a documented swallowing dysfunction on VFSE. Eighty-eight percent suffered from pharyngeal dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Characteristics of eating and swallowing problems in patients who have dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: DLB patients showed significantly higher scores than AD patients for "difficulty in swallowing foods," "difficulty in swallowing liquids," "coughing or choking when swallowing,"

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: New to this list is hypersomnia,14 usually presenting as excessive daytime sleepiness.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal daytime sleepiness in dementia with Lewy bodies compared to Alzheimer's disease using the Multiple Sleep Latency Test.
evidence.snippet: These data suggest that abnormal daytime sleepiness is a unique feature of DLB that does not depend on nighttime sleep fragmentation or the presence of the four cardinal DLB features.

evidence.reference_title: Daytime sleepiness in dementia with Lewy bodies is associated with neuronal depletion of the nucleus basalis of Meynert.
evidence.snippet: Sleepiness was present in 58% of the DLB group and those with daytime sleepiness had significantly lower neuron counts in the nucleus basalis of Meynert than their non-sleepy counterparts (p = 0.001).

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: DLB fluctuations have been described in detail previously1,2 and are typically delirium-like,e5 occurring as spontaneous alterations in cognition, attention, and arousal.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Fluctuations may also occur in advanced stages of other dementias, so they best predict DLB when they are present early.

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Cognitive fluctuations may be of lesser amplitude or frequency than in more severe disease.

evidence.reference_title: Quantifying fluctuation in dementia with Lewy bodies, Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia.
evidence.snippet: Patients with DLB had a greater prevalence and severity of FC than did patients with AD or VaD rated using clinical, attentional, and EEG measures. The 90-second cognitive and EEG trials demonstrated that FC occurs on a second-to-second basis in patients with DLB.

evidence.reference_title: The prevalence, assessment and associations of falls in dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: Multiple falls (>5) occurred in 37% of DLB patients and 6% of those with AD, often resulting in injury.

evidence.reference_title: Incidence and prediction of falls in dementia: a prospective study in older people.
evidence.snippet: In dementia, significant univariate predictors of sustaining at least one fall included diagnosis of Lewy body disorder (proportional hazard ratio (HR) adjusted for age and sex: 3.33, 2.11-5.26)

meta.association: GBA gene variants significantly increase risk for DLB

evidence.reference_title: Effect of GBA gene variants on clinical characteristics of dementia with Lewy bodies: a review and meta-analyses.
evidence.snippet: GBA variants increased the risk of DLB, especially N370S, E326K, and L444P which are strongly associated with DLB, but T369M was not. Patients harbouring GBA variants have an earlier age of onset, more severe cognitive impairment, and rapid symptom progression.

evidence.reference_title: An update on the genetics of dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: More recently, association and exome sequencing studies in larger groups have been conducted, and have shown that several variants in GBA and the APOE ε4 allele are important genetic risk factors for DLB.

evidence.reference_title: The Genetics of Dementia with Lewy Bodies: Current Understanding and Future Directions.
evidence.snippet: DLB shares risk loci with AD, in the APOE E4 allele, and with PD, in variation at GBA and SNCA.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Also new is hyposmia, which occurs earlier in DLB than in AD.

evidence.reference_title: Olfactory impairment in mild cognitive impairment with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: Participants with probable MCI-LB had worse olfaction than both MCI-AD (age-adjusted mean difference (B) = 2.05, 95% CI: 0.62-3.49, p = 0.005) and HC

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective survey of prodromal symptoms in dementia with Lewy bodies: comparison with Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: DLB patients exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of olfactory dysfunction, constipation, increased saliva and signs of rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder at the onset of memory loss than AD patients and normal controls.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Disproportionate attentional, executive function, and visual processing deficits relative to memory and naming are typical.

evidence.reference_title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms and cognitive profile in mild cognitive impairment with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: MCI-LB subjects scored lower on tests of attention, visuospatial function and verbal fluency.

evidence.reference_title: Nonamnestic mild cognitive impairment progresses to dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: In 88% of those who developed probable DLB, the baseline MCI diagnosis included attention and/or visuospatial deficits. Those who developed probable DLB were more likely to have baseline daytime sleepiness and subtle parkinsonism.

nodes.description: Levodopa can be tried for parkinsonism, but the motor response is smaller than in Parkinson disease, is seen in only a third to a half of patients, wanes faster, and carries a risk of worsening hallucinations and psychosis.

evidence.reference_title: The role of levodopa in the management of dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: L-dopa was generally well tolerated in DLB but produced a significant motor response in only about one third of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Levodopa response in dementia with lewy bodies: a 1-year follow-up study.
evidence.snippet: Positive response to the acute levodopa test was observed in 55% of DLB patients (acute DLB responders), and in 90% of PD patients (acute PD responders).

evidence.reference_title: Effects of dopaminergic medications on psychosis and motor function in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that dopaminergic medications have limited benefit in DLB because of the low likelihood of motor improvement and the risk of psychosis exacerbation.

nodes.description: Lewy bodies in the amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus and inferior temporal cortex (the transitional or limbic stage). High temporal-lobe Lewy body density relates to well-formed visual hallucinations, and early hallucinations to parahippocampal and inferior temporal density. Limbic and paralimbic dysfunction is also the correlate of misidentification delusions. It is reached from the brainstem in the caudo-rostral route and from the olfactory bulb and amygdala in the brain-first route.

evidence.reference_title: Visual hallucinations in Lewy body disease relate to Lewy bodies in the temporal lobe.
evidence.snippet: Cases with well-formed visual hallucinations had high densities of LB in the amygdala and parahippocampus, with early hallucinations relating to higher densities in parahippocampal and inferior temporal cortices.

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: In summary, the performance pattern of MCI-LB is best characterized as single- or multidomain nonamnestic MCI, or as multidomain amnestic MCI, whereas single-domain amnestic MCI is more likely to represent MCI-AD.

evidence.reference_title: Cognitive differences in dementia patients with autopsy-verified AD, Lewy body pathology, or both.
evidence.snippet: patients with Alzheimer disease (AD) alone and AD/Lewy body pathology (LBP) had more severe memory impairment than patients with LBP.

nodes.description: Diffuse neocortical Lewy bodies and neurites, the stage at which the full DLB syndrome is most reliably expressed. Clinical recognition of DLB rises with the extent of Lewy pathology, the diffuse stage carries a shorter illness than the limbic stage, and posterior and occipital association cortex dysfunction accompanies it.

evidence.reference_title: The limbic and neocortical contribution of α-synuclein, tau, and amyloid β to disease duration in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Patients with diffuse Lewy body disease had more severe pathology of each type and a shorter duration of illness than individuals with transitional Lewy body disease.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Further efforts are required to develop better interrater reliability59 for Lewy-related disease subtypes (olfactory bulb only, amygdala predominant, brainstem, limbic ... , and diffuse neocortical).

nodes.description: Progressive loss of neurons due to alpha-synuclein pathology and associated proteinopathies, leading to brain atrophy particularly in cortical and limbic regions. The neurodegeneration underlies the progressive cognitive decline and other clinical features of DLB.

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.
evidence.snippet: Intravitam PET and post-mortem studies revealed more pronounced cortical atrophy, elevated cortical and limbic Lewy pathologies.

nodes.description: Loss of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons (about half at autopsy) with loss of striatal dopamine and dopamine transporter sites. It can be minimal at presentation, when parkinsonism is absent and DAT imaging may be normal, and it accumulates over the course so that parkinsonism eventually occurs in more than 85% of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Striatal dopaminergic markers in dementia with Lewy bodies, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases: rostrocaudal distribution.
evidence.snippet: The homovanillic acid : dopamine ratio, a metabolic index, indicated compensatory increased turnover in Parkinson's disease, which was absent in DLB despite the loss of substantia nigra neurons (49%), dopamine and uptake sites.

evidence.reference_title: Autopsy validation of 123I-FP-CIT dopaminergic neuroimaging for the diagnosis of DLB.
evidence.snippet: While an abnormal 123I-FP-CIT scan strongly supports Lewy body disease, a normal scan does not exclude DLB with minimal brainstem involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Table 2 also includes an assessment of substantia nigra neuronal loss (none, mild, moderate, and severe) in order to subclassify cases into those likely or not to have parkinsonism (DLB-P and DLB-no P).

nodes.description: Hypometabolism and hypoperfusion of the visual association and parietal cortex, most pronounced in the visual association cortex relative to AD, with relative sparing of the posterior cingulate (the cingulate island sign) when tangle stage is low. It accompanies the visuoperceptual and visuospatial deficits and is one of the substrates of visual hallucinations.
nodes.id: Occipital and Parietal Association Cortex Dysfunction

evidence.reference_title: Glucose hypometabolism and neuropathological correlates in brains of dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Among widespread cortical regions showing glucose hypometabolism in the DLB group, the metabolic reduction was most pronounced in the visual association cortex compared to that in the AD group.

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies: basis of cingulate island sign.
evidence.snippet: CIS on FDG-PET is not associated with fibrillar β-amyloid deposition but indicates lower Braak NFT stage in patients with DLB.

nodes.description: Lewy-type alpha-synucleinopathy of the olfactory bulb, present in nearly all DLB cases at autopsy. It is the earliest stage of the unified staging scheme and the proposed entry point of the brain-first route, which continues into the amygdala and limbic lobe.

evidence.reference_title: Olfactory bulb alpha-synucleinopathy has high specificity and sensitivity for Lewy body disorders.
evidence.snippet: 97 and 91% for DLB versus elderly control

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: adds previously omitted categories of Lewy-related pathology including olfactory bulb only56 and amygdala predominant.57,58 Both of these are considered to be low-likelihood DLB but may in the future be useful in assessing prodromal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Autonomic dysfunction in dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.

evidence.reference_title: One year follow-up of parkinsonism in dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Motor subtype and cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease, Parkinson's disease with dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Mean UPDRS III scores deteriorated over the two year follow up in all patient groups, with decline in the PDD and DLB being more rapid (mean decline; controls = 1.6, PD = 5.1, PDD = 9.7 and DLB = 11.3 points, one way analysis of variance; F = 4.1, p = 0.008).

evidence.reference_title: Extrapyramidal features in Parkinson's disease with and without dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies: A cross-sectional comparative study.

nodes.description: Phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in the spinal cord, paraspinal sympathetic ganglia, vagus nerve, gastrointestinal tract and lower brainstem. evidence.reference_title: Multi-organ distribution of phosphorylated alpha-synuclein histopathology in subjects with Lewy body disorders.
evidence.snippet: The greatest densities and frequencies of PASH occurred in the spinal cord, followed by the paraspinal sympathetic ganglia, the vagus nerve, the gastrointestinal tract and endocrine organs.

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Patients with DLB frequently report a history of autonomic dysfunction at first clinic attendance, with 25%–50% complaining of one of more among constipation, orthostatic dizziness, urinary incontinence, erectile dysfunction, increased sweating, or increased saliva.

nodes.description: Lewy pathology in the coeruleus/subcoeruleus complex and related pontine and medullary nuclei that impose REM sleep atonia. evidence.reference_title: The coeruleus/subcoeruleus complex in idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder and subtypes in autopsy-confirmed dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Motor subtype and cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease, Parkinson's disease with dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies.

nodes.description: Excess muscle tone during REM sleep (REM sleep without atonia) on polysomnography. In a person with dementia and a history of RBD it carries a 90% or greater likelihood of an underlying synucleinopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: If the PSG shows REM sleep without atonia in a person with dementia and a history of RBD, there is a ≥90% likelihood of a synucleinopathy

evidence.reference_title: Prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies in REM sleep behavior disorder: A multicenter study.
evidence.snippet: Isolated/idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a powerful early predictor of dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) and Parkinson's disease (PD).

evidence.reference_title: Prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies in REM sleep behavior disorder: A multicenter study.
evidence.snippet: Cognitive decline in iRBD begins up to 10 years prior to phenoconversion. Attention and executive dysfunction are the strongest predictors of dementia in iRBD.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: It often begins many years before other symptoms, may become less vigorous or even quiescent over time

evidence.reference_title: The temporal onset of the core features in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) developed before the other core features in men and women.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathologic correlations in 172 cases of rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder with or without a coexisting neurologic disorder.
evidence.snippet: RBD preceded the onset of cognitive impairment, parkinsonism, or autonomic dysfunction in 87 (51%) patients by 10±12 (range, 1-61) years.

evidence.reference_title: Inclusion of RBD improves the diagnostic classification of dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Each of the 3 core features increased the odds of autopsy-confirmed DLB up to 2-fold, and RBD increased the odds by 6-fold.

nodes.description: Reduced hypocretin (orexin) immunoreactivity in the DLB neocortex at autopsy, correlating with hypersomnolence and with alpha-synuclein levels. The measurement is neocortical: the source reports hypocretin-immunoreactive fibers and neurons in cortex, and notes these may represent uptake from projecting fibers rather than local production. Whether the hypothalamic hypocretin neuron population is itself depleted in DLB was not examined, so no neuronal loss is asserted here and the contribution is proposed rather than established.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced hypocretin (orexin) levels in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: we show reduced neocortical hypocretin immunoreactivity in dementia with Lewy bodies patients correlating with hypersomnolence and alpha-synuclein levels.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced hypocretin (orexin) levels in dementia with Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: neuropathological hypocretin levels in Dementia with Lewy Bodies or Alzheimer's disease remain unexamined

evidence.reference_title: Prodromal Dementia With Lewy Bodies: Evolution of Symptoms and Predictors of Dementia Onset.
evidence.snippet: In the prodromal phase, 50% of DLB participants demonstrated gait disorder, 70% had rigidity, 20% endorsed visual hallucinations, and over 50% of participants endorsed REM sleep behavior disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Comparison of extrapyramidal signs in dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: The 58 DLB patients with complete data had more severe action tremor, body bradykinesia, difficulty arising from a chair, and facial expression, gait, and rigidity symptoms than PD patients (all P<0.001). Abnormal posture and tremor at rest did not differ.

evidence.reference_title: Neuroleptic sensitivity in patients with senile dementia of Lewy body type.

evidence.reference_title: Neuroleptic sensitivity in patients with senile dementia of Lewy body type.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Severe antipsychotic sensitivity is now listed as supportive, because reduced prescribing of D2 receptor blocking antipsychotics in DLB limits its diagnostic usefulness.

nodes.description: Putaminal dopamine falls by about 72% in DLB, but unlike Parkinson disease there is no compensatory increase in dopamine turnover and striatal D2 receptors are reduced rather than upregulated. This is the proposed basis for the poorer levodopa response and for severe antipsychotic sensitivity.
nodes.id: Striatal Dopamine Deficiency Without D2 Receptor Compensation

evidence.reference_title: Striatal dopaminergic markers in dementia with Lewy bodies, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases: rostrocaudal distribution.
evidence.snippet: In the caudal putamen, dopamine was reduced by 72% in DLB and by 90% in Parkinson's disease.

evidence.reference_title: Sensitivity and specificity of dopamine transporter imaging with 123I-FP-CIT SPECT in dementia with Lewy bodies: a phase III, multicentre study.
evidence.snippet: Abnormal scans had a mean sensitivity of 77.7% for detecting clinical probable DLB, with specificity of 90.4% for excluding non-DLB dementia, which was predominantly due to Alzheimer's disease.

nodes.description: Altered thalamic microstructure and cholinergic signalling with unstable thalamocortical rhythms, seen as posterior EEG slowing and moment-to-moment variability of the dominant frequency. This is the proposed substrate of fluctuating cognition and alertness; regional Lewy body density does not explain fluctuations.

evidence.reference_title: Visual hallucinations in Lewy body disease relate to Lewy bodies in the temporal lobe.
evidence.snippet: There was no association across groups between any neuropathological variable and the presence or absence of fluctuating cognition.

evidence.reference_title: Quantification and characterization of fluctuating cognition in dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease.
evidence.snippet: DLB patients had significantly more severe FC and more severe variability in attentional and slow electrocortical measures than either AD patients or normal controls in all time frames. Attentional and EEG variability also correlated significantly with independent clinical ratings of FC.

evidence.reference_title: Lower urinary tract symptoms in dementia with Lewy bodies, Parkinson disease, and Alzheimer disease.
evidence.snippet: detrusor overactivity in 92% of the patients with DLB

evidence.reference_title: The prevalence of autonomic symptoms in dementia and their association with physical activity, activities of daily living and quality of life.

evidence.reference_title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease-dementia: current concepts and controversies.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium.

evidence.reference_title: The temporal onset of the core features in dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Core Clinical Features Associated With Survival in Patients With Dementia With Lewy Bodies.
evidence.snippet: Shorter survival was associated with the development of VHs (hazard ratio [HR] 3.25, 95% CI 2.46-4.29) and parkinsonism (HR 2.28, 95% CI 1.54-3.39) during the disease course and VHs at the time of DLB diagnosis (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.18-2.16).

evidence.reference_title: Research criteria for the diagnosis of prodromal dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Pareidolias: complex visual illusions in dementia with Lewy bodies.

evidence.reference_title: What best differentiates Lewy body from Alzheimer's disease in early-stage dementia?
evidence.snippet: However, only a minority of DLB cases had either VH (22%), EPS (26%) or both (13%). In contrast, although not a core feature, visuospatial/constructional impairment was observed in most of the DLB cases (74%).

evidence.reference_title: Cognitive Decline in Mild Cognitive Impairment With Lewy Bodies or Alzheimer Disease: A Prospective Cohort Study.
evidence.snippet: Probable MCI-LB presented with less impaired recognition memory than MCI-AD, greater initial impairments in verbal fluency and perception of line orientation, and thereafter demonstrated an expedited decline in visuo-constructional functions in the ACE-R compared to MCI-AD.
